title: pinguicula vulgaris proles alpicola
intro: Pinguicula vulgaris proles alpicola, commonly known as the alpine butterwort, is a carnivorous plant species belonging to the Droseraceae family. It is native to the high-altitude regions of the Alps, where it grows in nutrient-poor soil and obtains essential nutrients by capturing and digesting insects. The alpine butterwort has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties that can help to soothe wounds and promote tissue repair. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and saponins, which contribute to its therapeutic actions of reducing inflammation, preventing infection, and promoting healing.
